MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JUNE 16, 2021

CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Stegura, Bacinski, Bain, Chan-Southwell,
  Radocchio, Schachter, Wisot, Uppal

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Larson, O’Malley, Yoo (alternate)

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Levi Sinkler, Administrative Aide
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING, APRIL 7, 2021

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
RADOCCHIO to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  APRIL 7, 2021

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  SCAQMD-MSRC GRANT UTILIZATION UPDATE AND SCE CHARGE READY
  PROGRAM

Administrative Aide Sinkler provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. This is an
update and overview on 1) a grant that was awarded by the SCAQMD for MSRC funds, and 2) a
program by SCE being launched next month. The SCAQMD grant is for two, Level 2, dual port
charging stations. The estimated total for the charging stations is $60K. The grant award is $30K
and the City’s direct cost is $30K, which is budgeted for FY 2021-2022.

The initial proposal was to install one dual charging station at Ernie Howlett Park and one dual
charging station at Highridge Park. The contractor determined that the infrastructure to add a dual
charging station at Highridge Park was not sufficient.

Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that SCE will be launching a program which would cover the
infrastructure for a minimum of two dual port chargers, but optimally five dual port chargers.
Additionally, the program would provide a rebate of 40% - 60% of the cost of the charging stations.
The City’s cost for five dual charging stations is estimated to be approximately, $29,300 to
$39,000 based on a high estimate, and $13,900 to $20,800 based on a low estimate.

Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that staff is seeking input on the following recommendations:
To move forward with the installation of two charging station at Ernie Howlett Park to meet the
requirements of the SCAQMD grant award; Apply for the SCE Charge Ready Program for any
one or more of the following locations: (2) dual port chargers at Highridge Park; (5) dual port
charging stations at Highridge Park; (5) dual charging stations at Ernie Howlett Park (offset by
AQMD grant); and, (5) dual charging stations at City Hall.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI has anyone done a study on where it would be used most.
Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that staff has not done any studies.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2021
 Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that the cost of the (5) dual port chargers versus (2) dual
chargers would be received by the City at a faster rate due to the cost to users. He also added
that something not taken into consideration earlier is that Ernie Howlett Park closes at dusk which
will limit overnight use.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked if there was consideration to install a charging station at the
site of the new nature center which will be coming to the corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and
Palos Verdes Drive East. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that for new construction, EV
charging stations are required. As part of this project, at least two charging stations will be
installed. At that time, other grant funds opportunities will be researched.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that, a few years ago, when the charging stations were
implemented, staff looked at where charging stations could be located. These included public
parking lots, parks, and City Hall. There has never been a formal usage analysis. Staff can bring
data to the EAC.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL stated that she uses the charging station at City Hall every week
and it is convenient because it is centralized. She is able to park and walk back home. Ernie
Howlett Park may not be as convenient and asked where at the park they would be located.
Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that they would be in the parking area across from the tennis
office. COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL stated that City Hall is a good site and believes it is used
quite frequently.

COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT asked if any part of the SCE program will be used to improve the
electric flow at Highridge Park. Administrative Aide Sinkler stated that staff was told and is their
understanding that there is a transformer towards the front of the park where SCE could pull
electricity from directly.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI stated that people should have something to do while they
are charging their vehicles and this should be factored into the location decision. There should be
an analysis that would help to determine which location is better than others.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN stated that distributing the locations of the charging stations would
help to see where the need for charging stations is throughout the city. If it is possible for SCE to
do the infrastructure at Highridge Park, she would endorse that. This part of the community would
feel left out if all the charging stations were installed at Ernie Howlett Park.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL asked if there is any idea where Rancho Palos Verdes is
installing EV charging stations since the Highridge area borders Rancho Palos Verdes.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that staff will look into this.

Administrative Aide Sinkler clarified that for the SCE Program, only one location may be chosen
and will follow-up with the program manager if more than one application, for multiple locations,
can be submitted.

COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL stated that (5) dual port charging stations would also reduce ten
parking spaces at Ernie Howlett Park. There should be consideration given to parking spaces.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI asked if there are charging stations at Peninsula Center.
Planning Manager Naughton stated that she does not believe there are any charging stations
there.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that there may be time and if the committee is available, to
meet before the July 12th application deadline.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN stated that the Highridge Park parking lot is heavily used.

A brief discussion ensued about the charging station locations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT made a motion, seconded by  COMMITTEE  MEMBER
RADOCCHIO,

  TO UTILIZE THE SCAQMD-MSRC GRANT FOR THE INSTALLATION OF TWO DUAL
  EV CHARGING STATIONS AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK. IN ADDITION, TO APPLY FOR
  THE SCE PROGRAM FOR TWO DUAL CHARGING STATIONS AT CITY HALL AND A
  BACK-UP APPLICATION FOR TWO DUAL CHARGING STATIONS AT HIGHRIDGE
  PARK.

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired about grants for charging stations at the South Coast
Botanic Gardens. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that it is not in our jurisdiction but the City
has a good relationship with them and that staff will look into any grants that may be available to
them.

B.  ASSEMBLY BILL 1346 - AIR POLLUTION: SMALL OFF-ROAD ENGINES

Planning Manager Naughton stated that this was brought to staff by Chair Stegura and this is an
important item since the EAC had discussed a prohibition of gas powered landscape equipment
and looking into the possibility of requiring electric equipment.

Planning Manager Naughton provided an overview of Assembly Bill 1346. If this bill were to pass,
the program would occur in two phases, which would begin in 2024 where exhaust and
evaporative emission standards for all new sales would be zero except for generators, and in
2028, where evaporative emission standards for any generators manufactured for sale in
California would be zero. As part of this, there will be a two-phase approach, until a time when
zero equipment would come down in cost, and battery back-ups are improved. Planning Manager
Naughton also provided a summary on the reasons for opposition to this assembly bill.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff will continue to monitor this.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI asked about a quote regarding emissions from gas powered
devices is equivalent to the emissions all the cars on the street and asked where it came from.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that she can look back in her notes for that information.

CHAIR STEGURA stated that the City of PVE already has an ordinance prohibiting gas leaf
blowers. The City decided not to do this and rather educate everyone on this prior to making any
changes.

C.  WEBSITE IMPROVEMENT AND ENERGY-RELATED PERMITS (VERBAL UPDATE)

CHAIR STEGURA stated that this came up when she could not find how to apply for a residential
EV charger on the City’s website.

Planning Manager Naughton provided an overview of how the Community Development page will
be revised to make it more intuitive and user friendly. Additional pages will be added, including a
page on Accessory Dwelling Units, Sustainability, and a Resources page.

CHAIR STEGURA suggested composting under Sustainability.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI asked about the number of ADUs. Planning Manager
Naughton stated that eight were applied for last year, but that none of the permits were issued in
the same year, due to varying reasons. There are approximately twenty existing ADUs and there
are approximately four that are currently in plan check.

CHAIR STEGURA stated that there was a suggestion to add a link for native and drought tolerant
plants for the website.

In response to a question by CHAIR STEGURA, Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City
of Rolling Hills Estates was the first to sign the joint powers authority to establish the Clean Power
Alliance (CPA) program. CHAIR STEGURA stated that at the last board meeting, the CPA entered
into a long-term contract with four energy providers, which will go a long way towards price stability
and supply stability.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City was able to work with CPA to understand how
the city’s participation is impacting greenhouse gas emissions reductions. The calculations for the
City specifically, the emissions factor for 100% renewable for residential and municipal facilities
is zero.

6.  CONSULTANT/STAFF ITEMS/COMMITTEE ITEMS

CHAIR STEGURA stated that there may be a report on EV charging stations for the next
agenda.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, JUNE 16, 2021
 7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR STEGURA adjourned the meeting at 8:14 p.m.
